blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting Questions From Hinsdale Homeowners

items.q: Can hydro jetting handle a clay lateral from the 1920s?
items.preview: If the pipe is intact, yes. We look first.
items.answer: If the camera shows the clay is intact, yes, at a pressure set for its condition. If a section is cracked or collapsed, we'll recommend a [repair](/hinsdale/sewer-repair) first.

items.q: Why jet instead of rodding again?
items.preview: Rodding leaves root growth on the walls. Jetting removes it.
items.answer: A rodding cable cuts a channel through the roots. Jetting strips the growth off the pipe wall, so the line stays open longer.

items.q: Does jetting help a kitchen line in an older home?
items.answer: Yes. Decades of grease in an original kitchen line is one of the best uses for jetting.

items.q: Will jetting make a mess in the house?
items.preview: We work from the cleanout and protect the area.
items.answer: We work from the cleanout whenever we can and protect the floors around it.

items.q: What does hydro jetting cost in Hinsdale?
items.preview: That depends on the line. You'll see a flat price first.
items.answer: That depends on the line length, access and how much buildup there is. You'll see a flat-rate price before we start.
